1.e4 d5 2.exd5 c6.name: Scandinavian Defence: Blackburne–Kloosterboer Gambit
1.e4 d5 2.exd5 c6.background: Joseph Blackburne played it successfully on at least one occasion, but after 3.dxc6 it is thought to be unsound and is almost never seen in master-level play.

1.e4 d5 2.exd5 c6 3.dxc6.strategy: Takes the second pawn offered. White is now two pawns up, and the gambit is unsound: Black has only some development to show for the material, which White can answer by calmly completing its own.

1.e4 d5 2.exd5 c6 3.dxc6 Nxc6.strategy: Recaptures with a developing move and settles for a pawn deficit instead of two. The knight takes a central post and the bishop on c8 is free, but Black has no d-pawn and must make quick development and open lines count for the pawn.
1.e4 d5 2.exd5 c6 3.dxc6 Nxc6.name: Scandinavian Defence: Blackburne Gambit

1.e4 d5 2.exd5 c6 3.dxc6 e5.strategy: Gives up a second pawn for open lines for the king's bishop and the queen, with no concrete threat to show for it. White is two pawns ahead, and the advanced pawn on c6 cramps Black by attacking b7 and d7, so White simply develops.
1.e4 d5 2.exd5 c6 3.dxc6 e5.name: Scandinavian Defence: Kloosterboer Gambit
